views.markdown:
**No ads, skip the sponsored parts, background playback** — in Arabic or English.

Hooked on YouTube's model and service layer rather than its views: views get renamed between releases and a tweak that hooks them quietly stops working. A player response does not.

Tested on YouTube **21.30.5**. Nothing is pinned to a version number: every class is looked up at runtime and skipped if it is not there. Hold two fingers anywhere for the settings, and the diagnostics page says what attached to your build.

Stopped at three points, because ads arrive by three routes and blocking one does nothing about the others. The app stops asking for ads at all, so they are never sent rather than sent and hidden; promoted rows are dropped from the feed by the identifier YouTube's own servers attach to them; and the player refuses ads before a video, in the middle of one, and the kind stitched into the stream itself.

Paid plugs, self-promotion and subscribe reminders are jumped over using segments other viewers submitted to SponsorBlock. A short line names what was skipped and offers an undo, and each segment is coloured on the progress bar so you can see what is coming. Eight categories, each with its own switch — intros, endcards, recaps and tangents stay off until you turn them on, because somebody chose to make that content.

SponsorBlock offers two ways to ask, and this uses the one that sends only the first four characters of the video's fingerprint — so the reply covers many videos and the server cannot tell which one you are watching. Nothing is requested at all when the feature is off, or when every category is off.
Audio keeps going when you leave the app or lock the screen.
Silence the prompt to update, since updating replaces the app and removes this tweak. And optionally hide the paid-promotion banner — off by default, because it is a disclosure.

Hold two fingers anywhere in YouTube. Arabic and English with right-to-left layout, and a card at the top saying whether everything actually attached to your build. The report is also written to Documents/AlbrhiYT-report.txt, so it is readable even if nothing else worked.

• **0.10.1 downloaded the same file over and over.**
• YouTube's playlists list each piece as *a range of bytes inside one file*, not as a file of its own.
• Now that line is understood, and it makes things simpler rather than harder: when the pieces are all ranges of one file, **that file is the video**.
• The report also says what shape the playlist turned out to have — how many entries, how many actual addresses, whether ranges are used.
• Fixes the build of 0.10.0, which never shipped.

• **Saving videos, at last.**
• What made it possible was the report from 0.9.2, and it is worth saying what it found: every individual quality on this build arrives without an address, but **the…
• That is also where every other tweak that can save videos ends up.
• **This does not.**
• Qualities that would download and then refuse to play are filtered out before you are offered them, not after.

_Free and open source. Segment data from SponsorBlock (sponsor.ajay.app), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The coloured markers are derived from iSponsorBlock by Galactic Dev, GPLv3. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by YouTube or Google._
